title: 1987 AHSME Problem 14
statement: \(ABCD\) is a square and \(M\) and \(N\) are the midpoints of \(BC\) and \(CD,\) respectively. Then \(\sin\theta=\)

solutions.text:
Take the square to have side \(2,\) with \(A=(0,0),\ M=(1,2),\) and \(N=(2,1).\) Then \[ \begin{aligned} \sin\theta &=\frac{|\det((1,2),(2,1))|} {\sqrt5\sqrt5}\\ &=\frac{|1-4|}{5} =\frac35. \end{aligned} \]

Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Assign coordinates to the square and write vectors \(\overrightarrow{AM}\) and \(\overrightarrow{AN}\)
Use the determinant formula for the sine of the angle between two vectors
